results.title: Implementation challenges that hinder the strategic use of ...
results.content: Overall, it is critical that governments establish sound data governance and management activities to succeed in adopting AI — although only 59% of OECD countries have a data strategy in place for the public sector, with even fewer providing actionable guidance for implementation [(OECD, 2024[24])](/en/publications/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_795de142-en/full-report/implementation-challenges-that-hinder-the-strategic-use-of-ai-in-government_05cfe2bb.html#Kappa_1a89ed5e_6aa383bb80). The enterprise version Microsoft 365 Copilot costs USD 30 per month, for example.5 Thus, a government running a pilot project comparable to Australia’s six-month pilot of 7 600 staff across 60 agencies [(2024[57])](/en/publications/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_795de142-en/full-report/implementation-challenges-that-hinder-the-strategic-use-of-ai-in-government_05cfe2bb.html#Aus_6aa383bb80) could estimate costs to be around USD 1.37 million for licenses alone; that does not include additions such as staff time for pilot administration and reporting results, as well as other overhead. For instance, Chinese Taipei invested USD 7.4 million to develop its own foundation model called Trustworthy AI Dialogue Engine (TAIDE), which uses Meta’s Llama open-source models [(Creery, 2024[62])](/en/publications/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_795de142-en/full-report/implementation-challenges-that-hinder-the-strategic-use-of-ai-in-government_05cfe2bb.html#Cre24_6aa383bb80).9. While these costs can seem high, they can pale in comparison to the significant research and development investments, staff costs and data gathering efforts needed to achieve the latest foundation models [(Stanford HAI, 2025[59])](/en/publications/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_795de142-en/full-report/implementation-challenges-that-hinder-the-strategic-use-of-ai-in-government_05cfe2bb.html#Sta25_6aa383bb80).
